title: Whiting on tomato and butter beans

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything here is a plain whole food or cupboard staple: onion, garlic, tomatoes, tinned butter beans, stock, spinach, fish, lemon and herbs.

supermarket.reason: Whiting fillets are rarely stocked at mainstream supermarkets like Tesco and usually need a fishmonger, so the reader may not find them; suggest an alternative such as pollock or cod.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a wide lidded pan, a knife and a board, and every technique is simple softening and simmering.

works.reason: The quantities suit four, the liquid is modest so it will not swim, and 6 to 8 minutes covered will cook thin whiting fillets through.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers slicing an onion and garlic and chopping 600g of tomatoes, and the step timings add up to about 30 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, basil and smoked paprika, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fresh tomatoes broken down into the sauce form the base of the dish, which suits early June.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fish, beans, tomatoes and spinach make a filling, balanced lunch a family would happily eat again.
